name: The Wise Men
title: Worshippers from the East
summary: The wise men, also known as the Magi, were learned men from the East who followed a star to Bethlehem to worship the newborn king of the Jews. They brought gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh, and their visit represents the Gentiles' recognition of Jesus as the Messiah.

keyEvents.title: The Star Appears
keyEvents.description: The wise men saw an unusual star in the east, which they interpreted as a sign that a new Jewish king had been born, and they set out on a long journey to find him.

keyEvents.title: Meeting with Herod
keyEvents.description: The wise men arrived in Jerusalem and asked for the newborn king, which made King Herod uneasy and led him to gather the scribes to find out where the Messiah was to be born.

keyEvents.title: The Worship of Jesus
keyEvents.description: The star led the wise men to the house where Jesus was, and they bowed down and worshiped him and gave him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

keyEvents.title: Warning in a Dream
keyEvents.description: God warned the wise men in a dream not to return to Herod, so they went back to their own country by another route.
